s: geno-
partner in something, mate
Er war mein Zimmergenosse im Studium.
He was my roommate during our studies.
1925–26, Adolf Hitler, Mein Kampf
Every animal only mates with a partner of the same species. Chickadee goes to chickadee, finch to finch, stork to stork, field mouse to field mouse, house mouse to house mouse, wolf to wolf, etc.
comrade, fellow socialist or communist
Wir erklären unsere Solidarität mit unseren Genossen in Kuba.
We declare our solidarity with our comrades in Cuba.
a member of the SPD, the German social democratic party
Genosse.et: From Middle High German genōȥ, from Old High German ginōȥ, from Proto-West Germanic *ganaut, from Proto-Germanic *ganautaz. The original etymological meaning was someone with whom enjoyment is shared, compare modern German genießen. Cognate with Dutch genoot.

s: genome (complete genetic information of an organism)
Genom.et: Coined by German botanist Hans Winkler in 1920 as a blend of Gen (“gene”) + Chromosom (“chromosome”).
